skill.name: code-instructor
skill.description: Teaches programming by building applications step by step, with line-by-line explanations, concept checks, debugging guidance, and beginner-friendly pacing.
skill.summary: Build applications while learning how each programming concept works.
skill.author: Emz1998

content.value_statement: Learning code can feel abstract when examples are disconnected from real projects. This skill teaches concepts while building working applications step by step.
actual_capabilities: Breaks application builds into beginner-friendly phases.
Explains code blocks with purpose, prerequisites, and execution flow.
Adapts pacing for beginner, intermediate, and advanced learners.
Uses bundled references for teaching patterns and common mistakes.
Provides a script that adds teaching markers to source files.
limitations: The annotator script inserts placeholders and does not understand full program semantics.
The skill focuses on teaching and may produce longer explanations than production workflows need.
It does not replace formal security review or performance testing.
Examples must still be verified in the target runtime.

use_cases.title: Learn by Building a Small App
use_cases.description: Create a working project while learning syntax, control flow, and data handling in context.

use_cases.title: Explain an Existing Code File
use_cases.description: Turn unfamiliar code into a structured lesson with purpose, key concepts, and execution flow.

use_cases.title: Coach a Debugging Session
use_cases.description: Use errors as teaching moments by explaining causes, fixes, and reusable debugging patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Build My First App
prompt_templates.prompt: Teach me by building a simple todo app. Explain each step, each code block, and each concept before adding the next feature.

prompt_templates.title: Explain This Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this code as a lesson. Cover its purpose, prerequisites, execution flow, common mistakes, and practical next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Debug and Teach
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me debug this issue. Show what went wrong, why it happened, the fix, and the general pattern I should remember.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor With Rationale
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this feature while teaching the design tradeoffs. Explain architecture choices, testing concerns, and production risks.

output_examples.input: I want to build a calculator and understand every part.
output: A phased lesson plan from display to input handling.
Short explanations before each implementation step.
Common beginner mistakes for each concept.

output_examples.input: This function works, but I do not understand why.
output: A purpose statement for the function.
A plain-language explanation of the core concept.

output_examples.input: My React state update is not showing on screen.
output: An explanation of direct mutation versus immutable updates.
A corrected approach described in plain language.
A reusable debugging checklist for similar issues.

best_practices: Start with the smallest working version before adding complexity.
Ask for the learner level so explanations match prior knowledge.
Run and verify each meaningful change before continuing.
anti_patterns: Do not generate a full complex app before explaining the foundation.
Do not skip error explanations when debugging helps the lesson.
Do not use the annotator script on untrusted paths without review.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It teaches programming through guided application builds, code explanations, debugging, and incremental feature development.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover best?
faq.answer: It includes guidance for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and React, with general patterns for other languages.

faq.question: Can it help complete beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts with small working examples and explains syntax, concepts, and mistakes in simple terms.

faq.question: Can it help advanced developers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can discuss architecture, tradeoffs, refactoring, testing, and production concerns when requested.

faq.question: Does it run code automatically?
faq.answer: The skill recommends testing code after changes, but tool execution depends on the agent and user permissions.

faq.question: What is the annotator script for?
faq.answer: It adds teaching markers to a source file so learners can study code structure more easily.
